# nonNumber

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a number.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonNumber() — Checks whether a value is **not** a number. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonNumber<T>(value: T | number): value is T;
```

`nonNumber(value)` is the same test as `!isNumber(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

The test is `typeof value === "number"`, which `NaN` and both infinities satisfy. Use `isFloat`, `isInteger` or `isNaN` when those cases have to be told apart.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type          | Description         |
| :-------- | :------------ | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| number` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a number; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonNumber("1"); // => true
nonNumber(null); // => true
nonNumber(0); // => false
nonNumber(1.5); // => false
nonNumber(NaN); // => false
nonNumber(Infinity); // => false
```
